title: AI Memory Boom Forces Samsung to Cut Phone Output by 30%
summary:
Samsung reported a preliminary operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, even as its mobile business is estimated to have lost 1 trillion to 2 trillion won in the third quarter. This financial divergence stems from a corporate structure where the semiconductor division collects high profits from the AI memory boom while the separate smartphone unit must pay those elevated prices for components, erasing margins on budget and midrange Galaxy devices.

The mobile division has asked suppliers to reduce fourth quarter component deliveries by 20% to 30% to avoid selling low margin hardware and prevent excess inventory. Average purchase prices for mobile memory rose approximately 211% year over year, with LPDDR5X RAM specifically increasing by 175%. Samsung is now prioritizing premium models where higher hardware costs are easier to pass on to consumers.

selectedTweets.text:
Samsung’s AI memory business has become so profitable that it is now crushing the economics of its own smartphones.

Samsung’s mobile division reportedly asked suppliers to reduce fourth quarter component deliveries by 20% to 30%. This does not mean Samsung is cutting its entire annual smartphone production by 30% but rather means the company is reducing near term output more aggressively than usual because rising component costs have made some Galaxy phones barely profitable.  Samsung’s mobile memory purchase prices reportedly increased roughly 211% compared with last year’s average, while smartphone prices have not increased nearly enough to offset that. This hurts budget and midrange Galaxy devices the most because memory represents a much larger percentage of their total selling price.

Samsung may manufacture memory, but its semiconductor and smartphone divisions operate as separate businesses. The mobile division still absorbs the economic cost of expensive memory, while the semiconductor division benefits from selling that same memory at dramatically higher prices. This creates a bizarre situation where the AI boom is hurting one side of Samsung while supercharging the other. Analysts believe Samsung’s mobile business may have lost roughly 1 trillion to 2 trillion won in the third quarter, but the company still reported preliminary operating profit of 107.4 trillion won as AI driven memory profits exploded. Cutting smartphone production allows Samsung to avoid selling low margin devices, prevent excess inventory and prioritize premium models where higher costs are easier to pass on. Consumers could see higher Galaxy prices, fewer discounts and fewer high memory configurations, while Samsung increasingly focuses on profitability rather than defending every point of smartphone market share.

This is clearly negative for Samsung’s mobile business, but it could actually be bullish for Samsung overall. The company is effectively choosing to sell fewer marginally profitable phones while directing scarce memory toward AI customers willing to pay much higher prices.
